subject: Renal
vignette: A patient with a ureteral stone has distention of the renal pelvis and calyces proximal to the obstruction on ultrasound.
question: Which term best describes this finding?

options.text: Pyelonephritis
Renal cortical atrophy
Nephritic syndrome
Hydronephrosis
Nephrolithiasis

explanation_correct: Hydronephrosis is distention/dilation of the renal pelvis and/or calyces, most often caused by urinary tract obstruction such as stones, severe BPH, congenital obstructions, locally advanced cervical cancer, ureter injury, retroperitoneal fibrosis, or vesicoureteral reflux. Dilation occurs proximal to the site of pathology and can lead to compression and possible atrophy of the renal cortex and medulla.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pyelonephritis is an infection of the renal parenchyma and collecting system, not the anatomic dilation described here.
explanation_incorrect.B: Renal cortical atrophy is a possible late consequence of long-standing obstruction, not the term for the acute dilation itself.
explanation_incorrect.C: Nephritic syndrome is a glomerular process with hematuria and hypertension, not dilation of the collecting system.
explanation_incorrect.E: Nephrolithiasis refers to the stones themselves; the dilation of the pelvis and calyces proximal to a stone is hydronephrosis.

educationalObjective: Hydronephrosis is dilation of the renal pelvis and calyces proximal to a urinary tract obstruction.

subject: Renal
vignette: A patient with a single functioning kidney develops complete ureteral obstruction from a stone. Another otherwise healthy patient with two kidneys has a similar unilateral obstruction.
question: In which situation would serum creatinine be expected to rise as a result of the obstruction?

options.text: In unilateral obstruction with a normal contralateral kidney
When obstruction is bilateral or occurs in a patient with an obstructed solitary kidney
Only when the obstructed kidney also becomes infected
Never; serum creatinine is unaffected by urinary tract obstruction
Only when the obstruction is congenital rather than acquired

explanation_correct: Serum creatinine becomes elevated if obstruction is bilateral or if the patient has an obstructed solitary kidney, because total GFR falls. With unilateral obstruction and a normal contralateral kidney, creatinine often remains normal because the other kidney compensates. Prolonged obstruction leads to compression and possible atrophy of the renal cortex and medulla.

explanation_incorrect.A: With unilateral obstruction and a normal contralateral kidney, serum creatinine often remains normal because the unaffected kidney maintains overall GFR.
explanation_incorrect.C: Infection (pyelonephritis) is a complication of obstruction, but whether creatinine rises depends on bilateral or solitary-kidney involvement, not on infection.
explanation_incorrect.D: Obstruction can impair GFR and raise creatinine when it is bilateral or involves a solitary kidney, so the statement is false.
explanation_incorrect.E: Whether the obstruction is congenital or acquired does not determine the creatinine response; bilateral or solitary-kidney involvement does.

educationalObjective: Serum creatinine rises with bilateral obstruction or obstruction of a solitary kidney, not with unilateral obstruction and a normal contralateral kidney.

subject: Renal
vignette: A 55-year-old woman has a stone impacted in the distal ureter just above the ureterovesical junction. CT urography is performed to assess the extent of obstruction.
question: Which of the following best describes the expected location of dilation and its mechanism?

options.text: Dilation of the bladder and urethra distal to the stone with cortical sparing
Dilation limited to the renal cortex with sparing of the pelvis and calyces
Dilation of the ureter, renal pelvis, and calyces proximal to the stone due to back pressure
Global renal atrophy without any dilation because the obstruction is partial
Dilation only of the contralateral kidney from compensatory hyperfiltration

explanation_correct: In urinary tract obstruction, dilation occurs proximal to the site of pathology due to back pressure of urine. A distal ureteral stone therefore causes dilation of the ureter above the stone, the renal pelvis, and the calyces, producing hydronephrosis. With persistent obstruction, compression leads to atrophy of the renal cortex and medulla.

explanation_incorrect.A: Structures distal to the stone (bladder, urethra) are downstream and are not dilated by back pressure from the obstruction.
explanation_incorrect.B: The renal pelvis and calyces are the primary structures that dilate; the cortex is not the site of dilation and may instead undergo compression and atrophy.
explanation_incorrect.D: Even partial obstruction typically produces some proximal dilation; cortical and medullary atrophy is a late consequence rather than a replacement for dilation.
explanation_incorrect.E: The contralateral kidney may undergo compensatory hypertrophy but does not dilate from a unilateral distal ureteral obstruction.

educationalObjective: Obstruction causes dilation proximal to the lesion; a distal ureteral stone dilates the ureter, pelvis, and calyces (hydronephrosis).

subject: Renal
vignette: A 60-year-old woman with locally advanced cervical cancer develops flank pain and a rising serum creatinine. Ultrasound shows dilation of the renal pelvis and calyces; no stone is visible.
question: Which of the following best explains the hydronephrosis?

options.text: Extrinsic compression/obstruction of the urinary tract by the locally advanced tumor
Autoimmune deposition of immune complexes within the glomeruli
Nonenzymatic glycation of matrix proteins from long-standing hyperglycemia
Detrusor overactivity causing urgency incontinence
Amyloid deposition within the renal mesangium

explanation_correct: Locally advanced cervical cancer is a recognized cause of hydronephrosis through compression or invasion of the urinary tract. Other causes include urinary stones, severe BPH, congenital obstructions, ureter injury, retroperitoneal fibrosis, and vesicoureteral reflux. If the obstruction is bilateral or involves a solitary kidney, serum creatinine rises.

explanation_incorrect.B: Immune-complex deposition produces glomerulonephritis with hematuria and proteinuria, not obstructive dilation of the pelvis and calyces.
explanation_incorrect.C: Nonenzymatic glycation from hyperglycemia causes diabetic glomerulonephropathy with nodular sclerosis, not mechanical obstruction.
explanation_incorrect.D: Detrusor overactivity causes urgency incontinence with leakage, not hydronephrosis from an obstructing pelvic tumor.
explanation_incorrect.E: Amyloid deposition in the mesangium causes nephrotic syndrome with Congo red positivity, not obstructive dilation from cervical cancer.

educationalObjective: Locally advanced cervical cancer can cause hydronephrosis by extrinsic urinary tract obstruction; other causes include stones, BPH, and retroperitoneal fibrosis.
